word:greek-nt:G0050.explanation: Agnoeō means not to know or to be ignorant of a person, thing, or fact. It is used when people do not understand a saying. It can also describe worship done in ignorance.

word:greek-nt:G0102.explanation: Adynatos means impossible. It can also describe a person as unable or incapable, including someone unable to walk.

word:greek-nt:G0177.explanation: This word means “uncovered,” describing something exposed rather than covered or veiled. It functions as a descriptive term, identifying a condition in which a covering is absent. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in 1 Corinthians 11. Its basic meaning remains focused on the lack of a covering; the exact significance of that condition in either verse depends on the surrounding passage and its discussion. The word therefore points plainly to being without covering, while the context determines what kind of covering is in view.

word:greek-nt:G0196«G0197.explanation: ἀκριβέστερον means accurately, or more exactly.

word:greek-nt:G0199.explanation: This word means “accurately” or “exactly,” expressing careful precision rather than a rough or uncertain account. It can describe giving information correctly, learning or teaching something with close attention, or acting with careful awareness. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs five times, so it is an established word for precision across several kinds of statements. Its precise force in any individual verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central idea remains doing or describing something with exactness.

word:greek-nt:G0245.explanation: Allotrios means belonging to another. It can also refer to a stranger. It can describe something foreign or strange.

word:greek-nt:G0292.explanation: Amynomai means to defend or ward off.

word:greek-nt:G0344.explanation: Anakampto means to return. It can also mean to turn back.

word:greek-nt:G0388.explanation: This word means “to crucify again” or “to recrucify.” It describes the act of putting someone on a cross again, expressing repetition of crucifixion rather than a first crucifixion. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Hebrews 6:6. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself clearly points to crucifixion repeated or treated as happening again.

word:greek-nt:G0418.explanation: This word means “impossible”: something that cannot happen or cannot be done. It expresses the absence of possibility rather than describing a person, object, or action by itself. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Luke 17:1. Its precise force there depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but its basic meaning remains clear: the matter being described cannot be avoided, accomplished, or brought about, according to the context. The word therefore marks a firm limit of possibility.

word:greek-nt:G0506.explanation: Anypotaktos means unruly or insubordinate—someone not subject to rule.

word:greek-nt:G0627.explanation: Apologia means a verbal defense, especially an answer given when someone is accused.

word:greek-nt:G0652.explanation: Apostolos means a messenger, envoy, or delegate sent to represent another. Scripture calls the twelve apostles, and it also calls Barnabas and Paul apostles.

word:greek-nt:G0731.explanation: Arrētos means unspeakable or inexpressible—something not to be uttered.

word:greek-nt:G0865.explanation: Aphilagathos means not loving what is good.

word:greek-nt:G0991.explanation: Blepo means to look or see.

word:greek-nt:G1138.explanation: Dauid is the personal name David.

word:greek-nt:G1163.explanation: Dei means necessary or required, expressing what must happen or what ought to be done.

word:greek-nt:G1264.explanation: This word means “to argue vigorously” or “to contend sharply,” describing an intense verbal dispute rather than a calm discussion. It presents people actively opposing one another in argument. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 23:9. The surrounding verse is needed to determine the precise force of the dispute there, but the word itself emphasizes strong, earnest contention. Its single recorded use makes this a focused term rather than a broad word for ordinary conversation.

word:greek-nt:G1361.explanation: Diotrephes is a personal name, identifying a particular man rather than expressing a general idea, action, or quality. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 3 John 1:9. Because it is a name, its basic meaning is the individual it identifies; the surrounding passage is needed to understand what is said about him there. English translations retain the name as “Diotrephes.”

word:greek-nt:G1435.explanation: Dōron means a gift or present. In a worship context, it can specifically refer to a sacrifice brought as an offering.

word:greek-nt:G1479.explanation: Ethelothrēskia means arbitrary or self-imposed worship.

word:greek-nt:G1497.explanation: Eidolon means an idol or false god.

word:greek-nt:G1570.explanation: Ekthetos means cast out or abandoned.

word:greek-nt:G1633.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to go out,” describing movement from one place or situation to another. It focuses on leaving or going outside rather than remaining where one is. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Luke 21:21. Its precise force in that verse is understood from the surrounding sentence, but its basic meaning is a direct action of going out or departing.

word:greek-nt:G1804.explanation: Exangellō means to announce publicly or proclaim.

word:greek-nt:G1893.explanation: Epei means since or because when it connects a statement with its reason. It can also mean when or after, marking a time. It can also mean otherwise when presenting an alternative.

word:greek-nt:G1941.explanation: Epikaleō means to call upon someone. It can also mean to call someone by an additional name, as when Simon was called Peter.

word:greek-nt:G2012.explanation: Epitropos means a steward or manager. It can also mean a guardian.

word:greek-nt:G2089.explanation: Eti means still or yet when something continues in time. It can also mean further or more when something additional is being considered.

word:greek-nt:G2203.explanation: Zeus is the name of the deity called Zeus. In the Greek New Testament, this word functions as a personal name rather than a general description or action. It occurs twice, both times in Acts 14:12–13. The word identifies the figure being named, while the surrounding passage determines what is being said about him in those verses. Its meaning is therefore direct and specific: Zeus, a named religious figure referenced in the New Testament account.

word:greek-nt:G2294.explanation: This word means courage, confidence, or encouragement—the inner strength that helps someone face a difficult situation without giving way. It points to a strengthening resolve rather than merely a passing feeling of bravery. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 28:15, and is rendered “courage.” Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is clear: receiving or possessing courage to continue faithfully when circumstances are challenging.

word:greek-nt:G2346.explanation: Thlibō means to press or press upon. It can also describe being pressed hard or afflicted.

word:greek-nt:G2416.explanation: Hierosyleō means to commit sacrilege or rob a temple.

word:greek-nt:G2539.explanation: Kaiper means although or though; it introduces a qualifying circumstance while the main statement remains true and in force.

word:greek-nt:G2654.explanation: Katanaliskō means to consume or use up, as fire consumes something.

word:greek-nt:G2698.explanation: Katatithemi means to lay down or deposit. It can also describe doing or granting a favor in hopes of receiving favor in return.

word:greek-nt:G2720.explanation: Kateuthunō means to make straight or direct. It can also mean to guide, including guiding feet into the way of peace.

word:greek-nt:G2786.explanation: Kephas is the personal name Cephas, given to Simon Peter.

word:greek-nt:G2823.explanation: Klibanos means an oven. It can also mean a furnace.

word:greek-nt:G2878.explanation: Korban means a gift or offering consecrated to God. It can also refer to the temple treasury.

word:greek-nt:G2917.explanation: Krima means a judgment or verdict. It can also mean condemnation, an adverse verdict.

word:greek-nt:G2962.explanation: Kyrios means lord, master, or sir—a title for someone with authority. It may refer to a human master, as with a servant’s lord, or to Yahweh, as in the phrase “angel of Yahweh.”

word:greek-nt:G3019.explanation: Leuitēs means a Levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi.

word:greek-nt:G3055.explanation: This word means a quarrel, especially a quarrel about words. It describes contentious dispute centered on verbal arguments rather than a constructive search for truth. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at 1 Timothy 6:4. Its basic sense warns about the kind of argument that becomes focused on disputes over wording and turns discussion into conflict. The surrounding passage is needed to explain its particular force in that verse.

word:greek-nt:G3082.explanation: Lystra is a city in Lycaonia.

word:greek-nt:G3437.explanation: This word means a complaint or grievance—an expressed objection or matter of dissatisfaction. It names the complaint itself rather than the act of complaining. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at Colossians 3:13. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense is a complaint or grievance held against another person. The word therefore points to a stated cause for dissatisfaction that may need to be addressed in relationships among believers.

word:greek-nt:G3442.explanation: Monophthalmos means one-eyed, with only one eye.

word:greek-nt:G3510.explanation: Nephros means a kidney and can also refer to the inner emotional center, rendered here as “minds” or “reins.”

word:greek-nt:G3705.explanation: Horama means a vision or something seen.

word:greek-nt:G3749.explanation: Ostrakinos means made of clay or earthen.

word:greek-nt:G3860.explanation: Paradidōmi means to hand over or deliver. It can also mean to betray.

word:greek-nt:G3914.explanation: Paracheimazō means to pass the winter.

word:greek-nt:G3983.explanation: Peinao means to be hungry or to hunger. It can also mean to desire earnestly, as in hungering for righteousness.

word:greek-nt:G4010.explanation: Pergamos is the name of Pergamum, a city in Asia.

word:greek-nt:G4137.explanation: Plēroō means to fill. It also describes fulfilling what was spoken and completing a time.

word:greek-nt:G4142.explanation: Ploiaria means a boat or small boat.

word:greek-nt:G4195.explanation: Pontus is a geographical name referring to the region called Pontus, associated with the open sea. In the Greek New Testament, it functions as a place-name rather than describing an action, quality, or spiritual condition. The word occurs twice, in Acts and 1 Peter, and identifies people connected with that region. Its ordinary meaning is therefore the territorial name “Pontus,” while “open sea” helps express the name’s underlying sense.

word:greek-nt:G4205.explanation: Pornos means a fornicator, or a person who is sexually immoral.

word:greek-nt:G4249.explanation: Prizō means to saw or saw through.

word:greek-nt:G4566«G4567.explanation: This form is rendered “Satan” in Scripture.

word:greek-nt:G4601.explanation: Sigao means to be silent or to keep silence.

word:greek-nt:G4708.explanation: This word describes doing something “earnestly” or “more eagerly,” with heightened care, energy, or desire. It emphasizes a stronger degree of earnest action rather than merely indicating that an action occurs. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Philippians 2:28, so its broader range of use cannot be established from repeated passages. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central idea is increased eagerness or earnestness.

word:greek-nt:G4753.explanation: Strateuma means an army; it can also refer to a detachment of troops.

word:greek-nt:G4928.explanation: Synochē means distress, anguish, or anxiety.

word:greek-nt:G5080.explanation: Tēkō means to melt or be melted.

word:greek-nt:G5134.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “wound” or “wounds,” referring to bodily injuries. It is a noun that names the injuries themselves rather than the act of harming someone or the process of healing. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Luke 10:34. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context, but its central meaning remains straightforward: physical wounds or injuries received by a person.

word:greek-nt:G5291.explanation: This word means “to spread” or “to spread out.” It describes the action of laying something across an area or extending it outward. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Luke 19:36, so its normal meaning is clear even though the supplied verse text does not provide the surrounding details. The word presents spreading as an intentional action, rather than merely describing something already lying in place.

word:greek-nt:G5329.explanation: Phares is a personal name, also rendered Perez in English. The person named is a son of Judah.

word:greek-nt:G5365.explanation: This word means “love of money”—a strong attachment to wealth and a desire for money as an object of affection. It describes more than simply possessing or using money; it identifies the heart’s devotion to it. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, in 1 Timothy 6:10. Its precise force in that passage is understood from the surrounding verse and context, but its central meaning remains a love that makes money especially desired.

word:greek-nt:G5413.explanation: This word means a burden or load—something carried, endured, or placed upon someone. It is used for burdens in both ordinary and figurative settings, including responsibilities or difficulties that a person bears. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs six times across five verses, appearing in Matthew, Luke, Acts, and Galatians. Its precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding context, but the central idea remains something weighty that must be carried or borne.

word:greek-nt:G5448.explanation: Physioō means to inflate or puff up. It can also describe becoming arrogant or proud.

word:greek-nt:G5484.explanation: Charin means for the sake of, because of, or on account of. It can also appear as “therefore” when introducing a statement.

word:greek-nt:G6074.explanation: This word refers to an ancestor or forefather—a person from whom later generations descend. It points backward in a family line, identifying an earlier family member rather than describing a general age or social position. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Romans 4:1, and its ordinary sense is “forefather.” The word therefore directs attention to someone remembered as part of the ancestry of another person or people.
